task_intent: Elevate Tessera’s five word games with expressive native controls and matching wall compositions.

features.name: Letter Boxed
features.mobbin_query: Letter Boxed word game with letters on four sides of a square connected by lines and submit controls

references.observations: Connected word paths remain visible after submission. Finished words carry checkmarks; Undo and Hint stay directly below the board. Adapted for the square-letter chain, preserving twelve visible nodes.
A dominant complete puzzle with a compact input area beneath it keeps attention on the board. Applied a single inline draft and direct controls.
Active clue and keyboard have a clear hierarchy below the board. Used nearby contextual instructions rather than another popup.

references.title: Man, these New York Times games are hard! A computational perspective
references.observations: The original research describes different-side adjacency, chaining each new word from the previous ending, and complete letter coverage. These invariants are enforced in the native controls and production backend tests.

features.search_limitations: Mobbin returned adjacent path and crossword interfaces, not a dedicated Letter Boxed screen. NYT help and official game pages were blocked; used the cited original research rules.

features.name: Strands
features.mobbin_query: Strands word search game with a grid of letters connected by traced paths, theme clue and hint progress

references.observations: Continuous paths, confirmation checkmarks and the accepted-word ledger explain progress. Used visible connecting strokes and persistent found-word list.
Quiet dark letter grid, an anchored word prompt and a small segmented progress meter. Applied a large theme title, restrained blue/gold and three-part earned-hint meter.
Draft and Submit/Delete controls are separate from the completed game state. Kept an explicit Enter action so tracing can be corrected without losing a failed draft.

references.title: Man, these New York Times games are hard! A computational perspective
references.observations: The paper documents adjacent nonrepeating paths, the opposite-edge spangram, three-extra-word hint credits, then a second hint revealing the same path order. Implemented both hint stages with validated trace submissions.
Accessibility review entry point; native implementation includes VoiceOver cell labels/actions, a tap-button alternative to dragging, large controls, and Reduce Motion handling.

features.search_limitations: Mobbin returned related path and word-search interfaces, not a dedicated Strands screen. Apple HIG HTML was JavaScript-only; native accessibility decisions follow existing app conventions.
